metaDescription: Five 3-burner propane gas grills that list for under $200, compared on heat per square inch, cooking area, grate material, lid build and side space.
expertTake: The Char-Broil Classic 3-burner is the best overall pick because its 30,000 BTU over 360 square inches gives a sensible heat balance and its porcelain-coated grates clean easily. The Veralune is the value pick for anyone who needs more grate area. Anyone cooking for a crowd regularly should skip this tier and look at a larger grill with heavier castings.
introParagraphs: A three-burner propane barbecue is the default backyard cooker, and the cheapest ones differ less than the boxes suggest. They are a thin steel cabinet, a few stamped burners and a lid, so the real decision is how much heat each square inch of grate receives and how long the shell lasts.

Total BTU on its own says very little. What matters is heat per square inch of cooking area, the grate material and how well the lid holds heat. We worked through those numbers for each model and ranked them by how sensibly they balance. Prices move, and the $200 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

products.name: Char-Broil Classic 3-burner propane grill, 30,000 BTU, 360 sq in
products.description:
The Char-Broil Classic lists 30,000 BTU from stainless steel burners and 360 square inches of primary cooking area. Dividing the heat by the area gives about 83 BTU per square inch, which sits in the 80 to 100 range that cooks well without wasting propane. The listing says the primary area fits up to 12 burgers, a fair figure for a family dinner.

Porcelain-coated grates are easier to clean than bare iron and resist rust better, though the coating can chip if you scrape hard. Stainless burners resist corrosion longer than painted steel ones, which matters because burner failure is the typical year-three problem on a budget grill. A compact size makes it suitable for a small patio.

Set beside the Veralune, it has less grate area and fewer features, but a better-balanced heat. Because the shell is thin steel, it will not hold heat the way a heavy cast grill does, so keep the lid closed and preheat for ten minutes. Brush the grates after each cook, clean the grease tray regularly and cover the grill between uses. A quick test of the hose with soapy water at the start of each season takes a minute and catches the most dangerous fault. Keep a spare propane tank filled so a long cook does not end early.
products.bestFor: Families of three or four who want an uncomplicated, well-balanced grill.
cons: Thin steel shell loses heat in wind
Porcelain can chip if scraped hard

products.name: Veralune 3-burner propane grill, 36,000 BTU, 445 sq in, wheels
products.description:
The Veralune lists 36,000 BTU over 445 square inches of cooking area. That is about 81 BTU per square inch, nearly identical to the Char-Broil's balance but spread over a larger area, so it can cook more at once. Wheels make it easy to roll to a corner of the patio, which counts for a grill that is heavy once the propane tank is attached.

A larger area suits families of four to six, using the rule of thumb of about 70 to 80 square inches per person. Be careful with the total: brands often include a warming rack in the number, and a warming rack cannot sear. Check how much of the 445 square inches is main grate before you count on it for steaks.

Measured against the Char-Broil, it offers 85 more square inches at a similar heat ratio, but the shell and burners are likely to be less durable. Use it with the lid closed, watch for hot spots by cooking a layer of bread on the grates and keep the grease tray clean to avoid flare-ups. Because it is sold with wheels, lock the casters when you cook and never move it while it is hot. If one side runs hotter, rotate the food rather than turning up the burners.
products.bestFor: Families of four to six who want more grate for the money.
cons: Total area may include a warming rack
Shell and burners may be less durable

products.name: Nexgrill 3-burner propane grill, 27,000 BTU, 429 sq in, stainless lid
products.description:
Nexgrill pairs a stainless steel lid and a built-in thermometer with 429 square inches of cooking area and 27,000 BTU. The heat comes to about 63 BTU per square inch, which is low for the area, so the grill will cook more slowly and has less capacity for high-heat searing. That is acceptable for burgers, chicken and vegetables, but it means steaks take longer to brown.

The stainless lid resists rust better than painted steel and holds heat reasonably, and a built-in thermometer gives a rough guide to the temperature inside. Porcelain-coated steel grates are easy to clean but less effective at holding heat than cast iron. Side tables provide some working space, which matters for a grill with a large cooking area.

Against the Char-Broil, it has a bigger area and a nicer lid but weaker heat. If you cook mostly at moderate temperatures, that trade is fine. Preheat longer than you think, keep the lid closed and check the thermometer against a separate gauge. A lower heat ratio is not a flaw for slow cooking: chicken thighs, sausages and vegetables do well at medium heat. For steaks, finish with a sear on the hottest burner and a short rest.
products.bestFor: Moderate-heat cooking with a stainless lid and room to work.
cons: Only about 63 BTU per square inch

products.name: IdeaMaxx 3-burner propane grill, 38,200 BTU, 302 sq in, cast iron grates
products.description:
IdeaMaxx lists the highest output in this guide at 38,200 BTU, over a small 302 square inch cooking surface. That works out to about 126 BTU per square inch, well above the 80 to 100 sweet spot, which means the burners are working hard and the grill will run hot in the center. Cast iron grates hold heat well and give strong sear marks, which suits that heat level.

A high BTU rating over a small area is mostly a marketing number: it burns more propane for the same steak and often creates hot spots. If the figure is total output across all burners, the effective heat flux is lower, so treat the number cautiously. The foldable side shelves and compact 23.6 inch length make it a good portable option for a balcony or camping.

Next to the Char-Broil, it is smaller with more heat and cast iron grates. Season the grates with oil, keep them dry and use the two-zone approach by leaving one burner off. Watch for flare-ups and keep a squirt bottle handy. At this heat level, trim the fat from chops and sausages so drips do not ignite on the burners. Turn the burners to low and close the lid to smother a persistent flame.
products.bestFor: Small patios and balconies where searing and portability matter.
pros: Cast iron grates hold heat and sear well
Highest BTU rating in the list

products.name: GRILL DEPOTS 3-burner propane grill, 30,000 BTU, 252 sq in, side tables
products.description:
GRILL DEPOTS targets balconies, patios, couples and camping with a 252 square inch grill and 30,000 BTU. The ratio comes to about 119 BTU per square inch, which is above the sweet spot and mostly reflects the small cooking area. Porcelain-enameled cast iron grates are heavy and hold heat, giving good sear marks on steaks and chops.

Folding side tables help with prep space and make the grill easy to store. The size is sized for two or three people, so it is not suited to a family cookout. At roughly 70 to 80 square inches per person, it matches a couple very well.

Set beside the IdeaMaxx, it has less output with a similar area and the same cast iron advantage. Both are compact picks for small spaces. Preheat with the lid closed, use one burner as a cool zone and clean the cast iron grates while they are warm. Cover the grill between uses to protect the enamel.
products.bestFor: Couples on a balcony or patio who want cast iron sear marks.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Total BTU means little on its own. Divide the burner output by the primary cooking area. The Char-Broil lands near 83 BTU per square inch and the Veralune near 81, both in the 80 to 100 range that cooks well. The IdeaMaxx at about 126 and the GRILL DEPOTS at about 119 are above it, and the Nexgrill at about 63 is below. A figure well above 100 usually means a small grate and a lot of wasted propane. Check whether the listed BTU is the main burner total or includes a side burner or a warming rack burner, because that changes the ratio a lot. When in doubt, count only the burners under the main grate.

Brands often add a warming rack to the number, and you cannot sear on a warming rack. Compare primary grate area, and allow roughly 70 to 80 square inches per person eating. A family of four wants 300 to 450 square inches of real cooking surface. The Veralune and Nexgrill list about 445 and 429, and the compact grills list 252 to 302. A rough way to check is to lay out the food you actually cook: a dozen burgers need about 300 square inches with space between them, and a few whole chicken pieces plus corn on the cob need more. If you often cook for guests, buy for the busy weekend and not the quiet Tuesday.

Porcelain-coated steel is easy to clean and resists rust, but holds less heat. Cast iron holds heat and sears better, but it needs seasoning and dry storage to avoid rust. Porcelain-enameled cast iron combines the two, with the caution that chips expose iron. Choose by whether you value convenience or sear. Cast iron needs a thin coat of oil after each cook to stay rust-free, and it takes longer to heat up than thin steel. If you grill rarely and store the unit outside, the easy-care coating may serve you better than iron.

Stainless steel burners last longer than painted steel ones, and a thicker lid and firebox hold heat better in wind. At this price the shells are thin, so wind and cold air will drop the temperature. Burner failure and rust-through are typical year-three problems, so stainless burners and a stainless lid are worth looking for. A cover and a dry spot extend the life of any thin shell, and a quick wipe of the lid interior removes grease before it turns to flakes. Wind is the enemy of a thin cabinet, so place the unit with its back to the prevailing gusts.

A grill with at least two burners can run one on high and one off, giving a hot side for searing and a cool side for finishing. All five grills here have three burners. Two-zone cooking is more useful than any extra BTU, because it prevents burning the outside before the inside cooks. Thick chops, bone-in chicken and sausages all do best with a sear on the hot side and a finish on the cool side. With the lid closed, the cool side behaves like a small oven.

Side tables give you somewhere to put a platter, and folding ones make storage easier. Wheels matter more than they seem, since a grill with a full propane tank is heavy. Check the handle and wheels for sturdiness, and make sure the grill is stable on an uneven patio. Check how the propane tank hangs and whether the cabinet door closes tightly. Keep the tank upright and at least a few feet from any wall or heat source.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat balance
howWeEvaluated.description: We divided each listing's BTU by its cooking area. The Char-Broil and Veralune landed in the sensible range. The IdeaMaxx and GRILL DEPOTS were above it and the Nexgrill below.

howWeEvaluated.title: Usable area
howWeEvaluated.description: Primary grate area was compared with household size. The Veralune and Nexgrill offer the most space. The compact units suit couples.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grate and burner build
howWeEvaluated.description: Materials of grates, burners and lids were reviewed. Stainless burners and a stainless lid earned credit, as did cast iron for sear.

howWeEvaluated.title: Practical features
howWeEvaluated.description: Side tables, wheels and thermometers were considered. The Nexgrill's lid thermometer and the Veralune's wheels stood out.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cap compliance
howWeEvaluated.description: Every grill was verified under the $200 cap at the time of writing. We left out a portable single-burner unit that does not fit a three-burner comparison. Notes rely on the spec sheet and owner feedback patterns.

rows: Moderate heat with a nice lid

howToChoose.subheading: Cast Iron vs Porcelain Coated Steel

cards.label: Cast iron (IdeaMaxx, GRILL DEPOTS)
cards.text: Holds heat and sears well. It needs seasoning and dry storage.

cards.label: Porcelain-coated steel (Char-Broil, Nexgrill)
cards.text: Easy to clean and rust resistant. It holds less heat.

howToChoose.note: Choose cast iron for sear and coated steel for easy cleanup.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A grill that heats quickly, a primary area for about a dozen burgers and grates that clean easily.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Char-Broil fits about 12 burgers and cleans easily. The Veralune takes more at once.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cook for a crowd, want heavy castings or stainless burners with a long warranty. Those start at a higher cap.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You grill a few evenings a month. A balanced budget grill covers it.

maintenance.why: Burnt residue causes sticking and flare-ups. A warm grate cleans easily.
Grease causes flare-ups and fires. A clean tray is a safer grill.
Soapy water shows leaks. Replace a cracked hose.
Spider webs and debris block gas flow. Clean ports burn evenly.
Moisture rusts thin steel. A cover extends life.

faq.a: Not by itself. Heat per square inch matters, and about 80 to 100 BTU per square inch is a sensible range.

faq.q: How much grill area do I need?
faq.a: Allow roughly 70 to 80 square inches of primary grate per person eating. A family of four wants 300 to 450 square inches.

faq.q: Should I choose cast iron grates?
faq.a: If you want strong sear marks and will season them, yes. Porcelain-coated steel is easier to clean.

faq.q: How do I check for a gas leak?
faq.a: Brush soapy water on the hose and connections with the tank open. Bubbles mean a leak.

faq.q: How long will a budget grill last?
faq.a: Typically several seasons with care. Burners and thin shells are the usual failure points.
